note: What each bridge looks like, for drawing or AI image generation. 'from_sources' lists facts the cited pages state. 'confirm_with_photo' lists details the pages do not state; do not draw them as fact until checked. Colors marked verified are stated by a cited page or by data/bridge_names.json. Rule D-07: write in own words, no pasted text.

rules: Deck is one horizontal line at y=34, round caps, 4 px stroke.
Draw only the parts that make the bridge recognizable: towers, arch, truss peaks, cables.
At most 2 colors per icon: the bridge color and the water or ink color.
Cartoon-simple: rounded joins, no thin lines, readable at 24 px tall.
No text, no people, no cars.

layers.1: First pass: silhouette and icon rules (96 x 48).
layers.2: Second pass: named parts, proportions, details (192 x 96). Reference art used only to read shapes and spacing; nothing copied. Anything the cited pages do not state is marked in confidence.

river_view.view: From the south, looking north, centered on the Willamette. West is left, east is right. The nearest bridge is lowest in the picture.
river_view.spacing_note: River miles are not evenly spaced (St. Johns and Sellwood are far from the downtown group). The view uses even steps so every icon stays readable; show real distance in the data, not the picture.
river_view.perspective: Far bridges are narrower and shorter; the river narrows toward the top. Columbia is a wider, bluer band across the top.
not_in_view: Interstate Bridge and Glenn Jackson run north-south over the Columbia, so they are not seen side-on from here.
Blumenauer crosses I-84, not a river.
Burlington Northern rail bridge and Gibbs Street pedestrian bridge appear in the reference art but are not in data/bridges.json.
